text.p: The Australian pay television unit of United International Holdings Inc, AUSTAR, said on Thursday it had begun legal action against the joint venture between rival Optus Vision and Australis Media Ltd.

"This action has been taken to protect AUSTAR's rights under its franchise agreements, which give AUSTAR the exclusive rights to use and access Australis' satellite infrastructure in AUSTAR's franchise regions," AUSTAR said in a statement.
The infrastructure sharing deal Australis and Optus Vision was reached in September and has the approval of regulators.

An AUSTAR spokesman said his company was seeking an injuction in the New South Wales Supreme Court to prevent the satellite business being included in the joint venture, arguing this asset had been double sold as AUSTAR claimed exclusive rights to the transmission in the non-metropolitan regions.
The spokesman said AUSTAR lodged documents with the court on Wednesday and a hearing would be held on November 22.

The action was separate to that taken by the Foxtel pay tv consortium over the same issue, he said. Foxtel, owned by News Corp Ltd and state telecoms group Telstra Corp, began an action to unwind the infrastructure deal last month.
